pa_regulation_details.name: CCPA Title III limits employee wage garnishments to 25% of disposable earnings or amounts exceeding 30x federal minimum wage weekly, whichever is less, and prohibits employment discrimination based on garnishment status with $1,000 penalties
pa_regulation_details.summary: CCPA Title III limits employee wage garnishments to 25% of disposable earnings or amounts exceeding 30x federal minimum wage weekly, whichever is less, and prohibits employment discrimination based on garnishment status with $1,000 penalties.
pa_regulation_details.requirements:
## Garnishment Calculation Compliance
- Calculate maximum garnishment as lesser of 25% disposable earnings or amount exceeding $217.50 weekly
- Implement payroll systems ensuring accurate disposable earnings calculations after required legal deductions
- Establish procedures for handling multiple garnishment orders with proper priority sequencing

## Anti-Retaliation Protections
- Prohibit discharge, discipline, or discrimination against employees subject to garnishment for single indebtedness
- Train HR personnel on 15 U.S.C. § 1674 compliance requirements and $1,000 penalty provisions
- Document garnishment-related employment decisions to demonstrate compliance

## Multi-State Operations
- Review state garnishment laws in all operating jurisdictions for employee-favorable provisions
- Implement systems applying most protective garnishment limitations between federal and state law
- Maintain current knowledge of state law changes affecting garnishment calculations

pa_regulation_details.name: Pennsylvania statute requiring higher education institutions to ensure English language proficiency of all instructional faculty through assessment, testing, and student complaint procedures, with state funding penalties for non-compliance
pa_regulation_details.summary: Pennsylvania statute requiring higher education institutions to ensure English language proficiency of all instructional faculty through assessment, testing, and student complaint procedures, with state funding penalties for non-compliance.
pa_regulation_details.requirements:
## Core Assessment Requirements
- Conduct English proficiency testing for all new instructional faculty before classroom assignment
- Maintain TOEFL iBT speaking scores ≥26 or IELTS speaking band scores ≥8.0 for non-native speakers
- Implement institutional assessment protocols approved by Pennsylvania Department of Education
- Complete assessments within 30 days of hiring or appointment

## Student Complaint Procedures
- Establish formal complaint mechanisms for students to report instructor communication issues
- Investigate all formal complaints within 30-day timeframe
- Provide written responses to complainants with specific remedial actions
- Maintain appeal processes allowing Department of Education review

## Faculty Remediation Programs
- Provide English language improvement resources for faculty not meeting standards
- Complete remedial instruction within 12-month period
- Document all remediation efforts and outcomes
- Implement employment actions for faculty failing to achieve proficiency

## Record Maintenance
- Retain all proficiency test results and assessment documentation
- Maintain complaint records and institutional responses for five-year period
- Document all remedial actions and faculty improvement plans

pa_regulation_details.name: This regulation implements Pennsylvania's Graduation Rates Reporting Act, requiring all public educational institutions to submit comprehensive annual reports on graduation and retention rates
pa_regulation_details.summary: This regulation implements Pennsylvania's Graduation Rates Reporting Act, requiring all public educational institutions to submit comprehensive annual reports on graduation and retention rates. Reports must include demographic breakdowns, program-specific data, and employment outcomes. Institutions must use standardized cohort methodology and submit reports by March 15 annually. The Department of Education will compile statewide summaries and make data publicly available. Non-compliance may result in withheld state funding and required improvement plans.
requirements: Submit annual graduation rate reports with demographic disaggregation by gender, race, ethnicity, first-generation status, and financial aid status
Provide program-specific graduation rates for all degree and certificate programs offered by the institution
Report retention rates, transfer-out rates, and employment outcomes data for graduates within specified timeframes
Use standardized cohort methodology consistent with federal IPEDS reporting standards for data calculation
Maintain comprehensive student tracking systems and supporting documentation for all reported graduation rate data

pa_regulation_details.name: Pennsylvania Act requiring higher education institutions to disclose gifts exceeding $50,000 individually or $100,000 aggregate annually, with enhanced reporting for foreign contributions above $25,000, enforced through state audits and funding penalties
pa_regulation_details.summary: Pennsylvania Act requiring higher education institutions to disclose gifts exceeding $50,000 individually or $100,000 aggregate annually, with enhanced reporting for foreign contributions above $25,000, enforced through state audits and funding penalties.
pa_regulation_details.requirements:
## Disclosure Thresholds
- Report individual gifts of $50,000 or more from any single source
- Disclose aggregate contributions of $100,000+ per donor within fiscal year
- Enhanced reporting for foreign gifts exceeding $25,000 under 24 P.S. § 2510-A(d)

## Record Maintenance
- Maintain comprehensive donor identification records
- Document gift value, purpose, and attached conditions
- Preserve supporting documentation for minimum seven years

## Public Reporting
- Submit annual disclosure reports to PA Department of Education
- Publish gift information on institutional website within 90 days of fiscal year-end
- Include gifts-in-kind, endowments, and naming rights agreements per 22 Pa. Code § 31.41

## Compliance Infrastructure
- Designate qualified gift disclosure officer
- Implement staff training programs on disclosure obligations
- Establish donor notification procedures regarding transparency requirements

pa_regulation_details.name: 22 Pa
pa_regulation_details.summary: 22 Pa. Code Ch. 31 establishes comprehensive academic and operational standards for Pennsylvania higher education institutions. The regulation covers academic program quality, institutional governance, faculty qualifications, student services, facilities, and distance learning requirements. Institutions must maintain appropriate accreditation, demonstrate financial stability, provide adequate student support services, and ensure faculty meet terminal degree requirements. Compliance is monitored through annual reporting, periodic reviews, and site visits by the Pennsylvania Department of Education. Non-compliance may result in probationary status, operational restrictions, or loss of authorization. The regulation promotes educational quality, student protection, and institutional accountability across all degree-granting institutions operating in Pennsylvania.
pa_regulation_details.requirements:
• Maintain regional accreditation and specialized program accreditation where applicable
• Ensure 75% of credit hours are taught by appropriately qualified full-time faculty with terminal degrees
• Conduct comprehensive program reviews every five years with documented learning outcomes assessment
• Submit annual compliance reports including financial audits, student data, and program effectiveness metrics
• Maintain adequate financial reserves and demonstrate fiscal stability through multi-year financial planning
• Provide comprehensive student support services including academic advising, career counseling, and disability services
• Implement robust student complaint processes with annual reporting to the Department of Education
• Participate in statewide transfer articulation agreements and maintain transparent credit transfer policies
• Ensure physical facilities and technology infrastructure meet current educational and accessibility standards
• Maintain FERPA-compliant student records management with appropriate security measures

pa_regulation_details.name: Pennsylvania's Institutional Accreditation Requirements (22 Pa
pa_regulation_details.summary: Pennsylvania's Institutional Accreditation Requirements (22 Pa. Code Ch. 36) mandate that all degree-granting institutions obtain Department of Education authorization and maintain recognized accreditation. Key requirements include demonstrated financial stability through audited statements and surety bonds, qualified faculty with appropriate credentials, adequate physical facilities and learning resources, comprehensive student services, and transparent consumer disclosures. The Department conducts ongoing oversight through annual reporting, site visits, and complaint investigations. Non-compliance may result in warnings, probation, fines, or revocation of operating authority. Authorization renewal occurs every five years with comprehensive institutional review. Institutions must notify the Department of material changes and maintain detailed compliance documentation.
requirements: • Obtain and maintain regional or national accreditation from a U.S. Department of Education recognized accrediting agency
• Submit annual audited financial statements prepared by certified public accountants and maintain required surety bonds or escrow accounts
• Employ faculty with appropriate academic credentials (master's degree minimum for undergraduate instruction, doctoral for graduate programs)
• Maintain adequate physical facilities, library resources, and technological infrastructure to support educational programs
• Provide comprehensive student services including academic advising, financial aid administration, and accurate transcript maintenance
• Submit annual institutional reports including enrollment data, financial information, and program outcomes by specified deadlines
• Notify the Department within 30 days of any material changes to ownership, governance, financial status, or program offerings
• Maintain transparent consumer disclosures regarding program costs, graduation rates, and employment outcomes
• Develop and maintain teach-out plans and student record preservation procedures in case of institutional closure
• Renew institutional authorization every five years through comprehensive application process submitted 12 months before expiration

pa_regulation_details.name: The Pennsylvania Sexual Violence Education Act requires all public school districts to implement age-appropriate sexual violence prevention education programs from grades K-12
pa_regulation_details.summary: The Pennsylvania Sexual Violence Education Act requires all public school districts to implement age-appropriate sexual violence prevention education programs from grades K-12. Districts must use qualified instructors, trauma-informed approaches, and evidence-based curricula while maintaining parent notification requirements. Programs must address consent, healthy relationships, bystander intervention, and available resources. Schools must establish clear reporting protocols, collaborate with community partners, and maintain supportive environments that encourage disclosure of incidents.
requirements: Implement developmentally appropriate sexual violence prevention education for grades K-12 using state-approved, evidence-based curricula delivered by specially trained instructors
Establish clear parent/guardian notification procedures with advance notice of program content, material review opportunities, and opt-out provisions with alternative activities
Provide annual training for all school personnel on recognizing signs of sexual violence, responding to disclosures, and fulfilling mandatory reporting obligations
Collaborate with local sexual assault service providers, law enforcement, and community partners to enhance program effectiveness and student resource access
Maintain trauma-informed, inclusive programs that address the needs of all students regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, or disability status

pa_regulation_details.name: Pennsylvania Student Consumer Protection Standards under 22 Pa
pa_regulation_details.summary: Pennsylvania Student Consumer Protection Standards under 22 Pa. Code Chapter 40 establish comprehensive transparency and accountability requirements for higher education institutions. The regulation mandates accurate disclosure of program information, costs, and outcomes while prohibiting deceptive marketing practices. Institutions must maintain clear complaint resolution procedures, designate compliance officers, and provide detailed financial information including refund policies. Special provisions address online education, career programs, and institutional closure procedures. Enforcement includes monitoring, investigations, and progressive sanctions. Annual reporting and documentation requirements ensure ongoing compliance. These standards protect student consumers while maintaining educational quality and institutional integrity throughout Pennsylvania's higher education system.
pa_regulation_details.requirements:
• Designate a qualified compliance officer with direct access to senior leadership and authority to oversee consumer protection compliance
• Maintain current, accurate catalogs and websites with complete program information, requirements, graduation criteria, and time-to-completion estimates
• Provide detailed cost breakdowns including tuition, mandatory fees, living expenses, and program-specific costs with functioning net price calculators
• Establish clear, accessible student complaint resolution procedures with multiple review levels, reasonable timelines, and proper documentation
• Ensure all marketing materials and recruitment practices contain truthful, accurate information about programs, outcomes, and institutional achievements
• Implement comprehensive record-keeping systems maintaining student communications, financial transactions, and academic progress documentation for required retention periods
• Provide equivalent support services and clear technology requirements for online and distance education students
• Develop and maintain institutional closure and teach-out plans with appropriate notification procedures
• Submit required annual compliance reports, student outcome data, and financial stability indicators to the Pennsylvania Department of Education

pa_regulation_details.name: Pennsylvania's Uniform Crime Reporting Act requires higher education institutions with sworn police departments to submit monthly crime statistics to state authorities within ten days of month-end, encompassing detailed incident data
pa_regulation_details.summary: Pennsylvania's Uniform Crime Reporting Act requires higher education institutions with sworn police departments to submit monthly crime statistics to state authorities within ten days of month-end, encompassing detailed incident data.
pa_regulation_details.requirements:
## Crime Data Reporting
- Submit monthly UCR reports within 10 days of month conclusion per 18 Pa.C.S. § 9103
- Report all Part I offenses occurring within institutional jurisdiction
- Include arrest data for Part II offenses including drug, weapon, and liquor violations
- Utilize NIBRS format for detailed incident reporting as of January 2021

## Institutional Coverage
- Applies to institutions operating certified police departments under 22 Pa. Code § 1-3
- Campus security without arrest powers exempt from PUCRA requirements
- Coordinate reporting with federal Clery Act obligations

## Data Quality Standards
- Provide geographic location details for each reported incident
- Include victim demographics and offense circumstances
- Document bias incidents and hate crime classifications per Act 16 of 2020
- Maintain accuracy standards subject to Pennsylvania State Police audit

nj_regulation_details.name: New Jersey's Campus Sexual Assault Victim Bill of Rights mandates comprehensive protections for sexual assault victims at higher education institutions
nj_regulation_details.summary: New Jersey's Campus Sexual Assault Victim Bill of Rights mandates comprehensive protections for sexual assault victims at higher education institutions. The law requires colleges and universities to provide fair investigation procedures, support services including free counseling and medical care, trained personnel, confidentiality protections, and academic accommodations. Institutions must maintain clear policies, coordinate with law enforcement while respecting victim choice in reporting, and ensure disciplinary proceedings meet strict fairness standards within established timeframes.

nj_regulation_details.name: The New Jersey Anti-Hazing Law criminalizes hazing activities in educational institutions and student organizations, defining hazing as intentional actions causing mental or physical discomfort, embarrassment, or harassment
nj_regulation_details.summary: The New Jersey Anti-Hazing Law criminalizes hazing activities in educational institutions and student organizations, defining hazing as intentional actions causing mental or physical discomfort, embarrassment, or harassment. The law establishes criminal penalties ranging from disorderly persons offenses to third-degree crimes depending on severity. Educational institutions must implement anti-hazing policies, provide prevention education, investigate incidents, and maintain reporting procedures. The statute includes whistleblower protections, extends to off-campus activities, and explicitly states that consent is not a defense for hazing activities.

nj_regulation_details.name: N
nj_regulation_details.summary: N.J.A.C. 9A:1-1 establishes accreditation standards for New Jersey post-secondary institutions, requiring recognized accrediting agency approval, institutional stability, qualified faculty, adequate facilities, and financial viability. Institutions undergo comprehensive review cycles every ten years with interim monitoring. Standards address academic quality, student services, faculty requirements, financial accountability, and continuous improvement. Compliance monitoring includes annual reporting, site visits, and progressive sanctions for non-compliance, with appeals processes available.

nj_regulation_details.name: N
nj_regulation_details.summary: N.J.A.C. 9A:9-2 governs New Jersey's Tuition Aid Grant Program compliance, requiring participating institutions to verify student eligibility, maintain detailed records, accurately calculate and disburse awards, and submit regular compliance reports. The regulation establishes residency requirements, academic progress standards, refund procedures, and documentation retention requirements. Institutions must undergo periodic audits and face penalties for non-compliance including program suspension.

nj_regulation_details.name: N
nj_regulation_details.summary: N.J.S.A. 52:17B-5.1 requires New Jersey higher education institutions to report criminal incidents to state police using Uniform Crime Reporting standards. Institutions must designate trained officials to collect and submit crime data monthly, maintain public incident logs, and coordinate with local law enforcement. Reporting covers violent crimes, property crimes, drug offenses, and disciplinary violations occurring on campus and adjacent properties. Emergency incidents require 24-hour notification, with comprehensive annual reports due by March 1st.

nj_regulation_details.name: N
nj_regulation_details.summary: N.J.S.A. 18A:62-6 establishes tuition benefits for qualified New Jersey veterans and their dependents at state institutions of higher education. The program covers full tuition and fees at public institutions, with equivalent support at private colleges. Eligible participants include honorably discharged veterans who were New Jersey residents upon military entry, plus certain dependents of deceased or missing service members. Institutions must designate certified veterans' education officials, maintain comprehensive records, verify student eligibility and academic progress, coordinate with federal benefits, and provide veteran-supportive campus environments and services.
